Hi Rajesh — thanks, glad the demo helped. Quick reply with a compact plan and attached starter artifacts. High-level:

1) Pre-cutover (Day -1)
   - Confirm sandbox keys and a short smoke test (5 requests/min)
   - Upload mutual action plan to DocuSign (linked below)

2) Cutover window (2 hours)
   - Point 10% traffic to Redwood hosted endpoint (canary) for 20 mins; check latency/4xx/5xx
   - Shift to dedicated endpoint; monitor prefix cache warmup (we recommend warmups before full shift)

3) Post-cutover (Day +1)
   - Validate cost/latency metrics and turn on adaptive batching if throughput increases

Attached: lite-sdk-sample.go (Go snippet), rate-limit-matrix.xlsx (client-side token-bucket config), mutual-action-plan-v1.pdf (SoW stub).

Quick answers to your bullets:
- Endpoint selection: client should prefer regional hosted endpoint (us-west) with a fallback to your dedicated endpoint via preconfigured base-URL list. See sample init.
- Retries/timeouts: start conservative for auth paths (connect 200ms, request 1500ms, max retries 2 with exp backoff + jitter). For async or background flows, relax to 3s and 3 retries.
- Rate limits: client token-bucket with capacity equal to expected QPS for auth lane; we recommend a leaky/steady drain for steady-state and allow short bursts (burst factor 1.5).
- Migration: add new CNAME for cutover, keep old endpoint for 24h, and route 10->50->100.

If that works, propose Tue 11/2 09:00-11:00 PST as you suggested. Monica will run the PM/CS side; Kim will be on the call for runtime tweaks.

Hey team — adding the tactical checklist for the implementers. I've kept it tight so your devs can follow in-session.

Implementation Checklist (45-60 min run):
- Sandbox prep (10 min)
  - Confirm sandbox keys + region (us-west-2). Run smoke: curl -X POST https://sandbox.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -d '{"prompt":"ping"}'
- Client init (10 min)
  - Use attached lite-sdk-sample.go: shows initialization with prioritized endpoints and an easy toggle for dedicated base_url.
- Timeouts & retries (10 min)
  - Recommended: connect_timeout=250ms; read_timeout=1200ms for auth-critical flows; request_timeout=3000ms for batch/async.
  - Retries: max_retries=2 for sync auth; backoff: base=100ms, factor=2, jitter=0.2.
- Rate limiting (5 min)
  - Start with token-bucket: capacity=QPS_expected*2, refill_rate=QPS_expected, burst=1.5. If you already have client leaky-bucket infra, keep that and add a local in-memory token-bucket as a first layer.
- Cutover plan (5-10 min)
  - Add new CNAME: redwood-fastpay.prod -> redwood.hosting.region
  - Stage: 10% (20m), 50% (20m), 100% with monitoring (20m)

I'll own the mutual action plan DocuSign and post the signed copy to the Drive folder linked below. If you want, I can run the smoke tests for you during the first 10 minutes.

Rajesh / team — quick engineering notes and a tiny Go example inline to make cutover frictionless.

Key runtime guidance:
- Connection and socket timeouts: connect=200-300ms; socket/read=1.0-1.5s for auth endpoints. These keep tail latency tight.
- Retry policy:
  - Use exponential backoff with full-jitter (see: https://www.awsarchitectureblog.com/2015/03/backoff.html)
  - max_retries_sync=2 (status 429/503/504), max_retries_async=3
  - Do not retry on 4xx other than 429
- Backoff params: base=120ms, multiplier=2.0, jitter=0.25; cap=2s
- Client-side rate limiter: token-bucket with token_batching for bursts. If you can, maintain a sliding-window for outgoing QPS to avoid sudden spikes on our side.
- Caching: enable prefix/KV cache warmup for common prompts during canary to avoid cold-cache penalties. Pre-warm with 5-10 sample requests.

Inline Go snippet (very small):
